lesson.subject: maths
lesson.title: Adding and Subtracting 2-Digit Numbers
lesson.summary: Add and take away two 2-digit numbers by splitting them into tens and ones, including crossing a ten.
learning_objectives: Add two 2-digit numbers, even when I cross a ten
Take away two 2-digit numbers, even when I cross a ten
Solve word problems and find missing numbers

standards.text: Add and subtract a two-digit number and ones, and two two-digit numbers, using concrete objects, number lines and mental methods

success_criteria: I can split numbers into tens and ones to add
I can cross a ten when I add or take away
I can solve a story problem and check my answer
lesson.real_life: Counting mangoes at a market stall, pens in a shop, or how many dates are left at iftar.

warm_up.hint: The left digit is the tens.

blocks.text: Meet Zara and the mango stall

blocks.alt: Ripe mangoes in a box at a market stall with hand-written price signs
blocks.caption: Zara's uncle sells mangoes at a market stall.
blocks.credit: Photo by leila goodman on Unsplash
blocks.say: Meet Zara. She helps her uncle Bilal at his mango stall in Lahore. Mangoes, mangoes everywhere! Today Zara must count them all. We will help her. We will add and take away big numbers. We split them into tens and ones.

blocks.text: Stop 1: Split into tens and ones

blocks.markdown:
A **2-digit number** is made of **tens** and **ones**.

34 is 3 tens and 4 ones.

**Partition** means to split a number into parts.
blocks.say: Every two-digit number is made of tens and ones. Take thirty-four. It has three tens and four ones. A ten is a long rod. A one is a little square. Let's split thirty-four and twenty-three together.

scenes.caption: 34 = 3 tens and 4 ones.
scenes.say: Here is thirty-four. Three tens and four ones. Say it with me: three tens, four ones.

scenes.caption: 34 and 23, split into tens and ones.
scenes.say: Now here is twenty-three. Two tens and three ones. Do we count every single one? No way!

scenes.caption: 30 + 20 = 50. Five tens.
scenes.say: Add the tens first. Three tens and two tens make five tens. That is fifty.

scenes.caption: 4 + 3 = 7 ones. 50 + 7 = 57.
scenes.say: Now add the ones. Four ones and three ones make seven ones. Fifty and seven make fifty-seven!

question.prompt: How many tens are in the number 25?

blocks.text: Stop 2: Add the tens, then the ones

blocks.markdown:
**Add** the tens, then add the ones, then put them together.

25 + 14: 20 + 10 = 30 and 5 + 4 = 9, so the **total** is 39.
blocks.say: Here is the trick. Add the tens. Then add the ones. Then put the two answers together. Let's try twenty-five plus fourteen. Watch the frog hop along the number line.

scenes.caption: Start at 25.
scenes.say: The frog starts on twenty-five. Fourteen is one ten and four ones.

scenes.caption: + 10 makes 35.
scenes.say: Hop one ten. Twenty-five to thirty-five. That is the tens part.

scenes.caption: + 4 makes 39. 25 + 14 = 39.
scenes.say: Now hop four ones. Thirty-six, thirty-seven, thirty-eight, thirty-nine. The frog lands on thirty-nine!

question.prompt: What is 32 + 15? Add the tens, then the ones.

blocks.title: Zara fills a tray of ten
blocks.transcript: This is Zara. She helps her uncle Bilal at his mango stall in Lahore. Uncle has twenty-seven mangoes. A van brings sixteen more. How many mangoes now? Zara has a tray that holds ten. Twenty-seven is two full trays and seven loose. Zara picks three mangoes from the new box. Seven and three make ten! The box had sixteen. Three are gone. Thirteen are left. Now we have three full trays. That is thirty. Plus the thirteen in the box. Thirty and thirteen. Thirty plus ten is forty. Forty plus three is forty-three! Forty-three mangoes! When the ones go past nine, fill a ten first. Shukriya, Zara!
blocks.caption: Watch Zara cross a ten at the mango stall.

blocks.markdown:
When the ones make more than 9, you make a new **ten**.

This is called **crossing a ten**.
blocks.say: Zara has twenty-eight mangoes. Her uncle gives her fifteen more. Look at the ones. Eight and five make more than nine! That means a brand new ten is born. Watch the ten frames.

scenes.caption: 28 and 15.
scenes.say: Twenty-eight is two tens and eight ones. Fifteen is one ten and five ones.
Add the tens first. Two tens and one ten make three tens. That is thirty.

scenes.caption: 8 + 5 in ten frames.
scenes.say: Now the ones. Eight and five. Each ten frame holds only ten. Will they fit?

scenes.caption: 8 + 2 = 10, and 3 left.
scenes.say: Take two from the five to fill the first frame. That makes ten! Three are left over.
Eight and five make thirteen. That is one ten and three ones.
Now thirty and thirteen. Three tens and one more ten make four tens. Four tens and three ones is forty-three!

blocks.title: Make a tray of ten
blocks.goal: Zara has 8 mangoes. Her uncle gives her 5 more. Move 10 mangoes into the Tray of ten. How many are left over?

question.prompt: You add 7 + 6 and get 13. After you make a ten, how many ones are left?
question.hint: 13 is one ten and some ones.

blocks.markdown:
Keep one number **whole** and split the other.

28 + 15: 28 + 2 = 30, 30 + 10 = 40, 40 + 3 = 43.
blocks.say: Here is a speedy way. Keep twenty-eight whole. Split only the fifteen. Split fifteen into two, ten and three. Hop two to reach thirty. Hop ten to forty. Hop three more.

scenes.caption: Start at 28. 15 = 2 + 10 + 3.
scenes.say: The frog is on twenty-eight. Fifteen is the same as two, ten and three.
Hop two. Twenty-eight and two make thirty. Thirty is a friendly ten!
Now hop one whole ten. Thirty to forty.
Last, hop three. Forty-one, forty-two, forty-three. The frog lands on forty-three. It is the same answer!

blocks.markdown:
To **take away** is to make a number smaller.

63 - 24: take away 20 first, then take away 4.
blocks.say: Time for a take-away race! Uncle Bilal had sixty-three mangoes. He sold twenty-four. How many are left? To take away means to make a number smaller. Here is the trick. Split only the part you take away.

scenes.caption: 63 = 6 tens and 3 ones.
scenes.say: Sixty-three is six tens and three ones. We must take away twenty-four.
First take away the two tens. Four tens are left.

scenes.caption: Start at 43 and take away 4.
scenes.say: Now take away four more. The frog starts on forty-three.
Hop back three. That lands on forty. Forty is a friendly ten!
One more to go. Hop back one. Thirty-nine! Zara has thirty-nine mangoes left.

blocks.text: Stop 2: Take away across a ten

blocks.markdown:
Always start from the big number: 75 - 6.

75 - 5 = 70, then 70 - 1 = 69.
blocks.say: Careful with the ones! Look at seventy-five take away six. Do not do six take away five. The big number always comes first. Hop back five to reach seventy. Then hop back one more.

scenes.caption: Start at 75. Take away 6.
scenes.say: The frog is on seventy-five. We take away six.
Hop back five. Seventy-five take away five is seventy. That is a friendly ten.
We still have one to take away. Hop back one. Sixty-nine!

blocks.markdown:
A **missing number** is a number we need to find.

24 + ? = 41. Count up from 24 to 41.
blocks.say: Zara has twenty-four dates for iftar. Her uncle gives her some more. Now she has forty-one. How many did he give her? We do not know the number. That is the missing number. Count up from twenty-four to forty-one.

blocks.answer_markdown: 17. Adding and taking away are opposites, so 41 - 24 gives the missing number too.
